title: Choose the visual world for Rehearse (round 2)
question: Your brief: unique, fun, playful, inviting, trustworthy, game-like, friendly, arty, for teens and adults. The roll assigned The Sticker Book. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: The Sticker Book
options.lineage: die-cut sticker sheets, laptop sticker packs, collectible sticker albums
options.thesis: Every skill you practise becomes a bold die-cut sticker you earn, and your progress is a sticker sheet filling up.
options.viewport: A big friendly question in chunky type, with a sticker slapped on the corner of the input; below, your sticker sheet with empty outlines waiting to be earned.
options.risk: Can tip into childish if the stickers are cute mascots; it needs grown-up graphic sticker art, like laptop sticker packs.

raised.raise: A folded flag sticker marks exactly where you stopped, so you can always pick up again.
Earned stickers are joined by lines that light up, showing your path through the skills.
State is shown with marks, not only colour: a peeled corner means locked, a full sticker means earned.

options.label: The Community Zine
options.thesis: A handmade, two-ink riso print from your local community print shop: arty, warm, and clearly made for people, not a corporation.
options.viewport: Oversized headline overprinted in pink and blue, a doodled arrow pointing at the job input, a torn-edge notes card below.
options.risk: Arty zine styles are popular right now, so it's the more familiar of the two creative options.

options.label: Public Service Poster
options.thesis: Each screen is one bold poster with one clear instruction, like TAKE TWO.
options.viewport: A layered landscape (the climb to your job) with one big imperative caption: WHAT JOB ARE YOU AIMING FOR?
options.case: Very clear and trustworthy, feels like a free public service; less game-like and more American-heritage than playful.
options.risk: Can feel old-fashioned or heavy if the illustrations are weak.

options.label: Sneaker Box Wall
options.lineage: sneaker archive walls and shoe boxes
options.thesis: Your saved answers are a wall of labelled boxes; open one to see the answer folded in tissue.
options.viewport: A wall of stacked boxes, one pulled half out with your next question on its end label.
options.case: Teens get it instantly and the Remember tab maps beautifully; adults and non-sneaker fans may not identify with it.
options.risk: Streetwear culture can feel exclusive to some users.

options.label: Film Cutting Bench
options.thesis: Steps as punched film frames along a rail.
options.viewport: A perforated film rail across the screen.
options.case: Nobody practising for a job interview identifies with film editing.
options.kept: A flag marking where you stopped.

options.label: Darkroom Exposure Record
options.thesis: Overlapping translucent sheets with hatch marks.
options.viewport: Stacked sheets over a grey ramp.
options.case: Technical and cold for anxious first-time job seekers.
options.kept: Show state with marks, not only colour.

options.label: Alphabet Storm
options.case: Beautiful, but moving text hurts readability for people with low literacy or dyslexia.

options.label: Neon Wiring Grid
options.thesis: Neon line diagrams on a strict grid.
options.case: Cool and graphic but cold, not friendly or inviting.
options.kept: Progress lines that light up between completed steps.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A friendly gamified learning app: bright green, rounded cards, mascot energy.
canonCard.viewport: Big green start button, XP bar, streak counter.
